Author, per the Draft Forum's new policy: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-10629348/new-draft-forum-policies authors who have not yet posted a successful mainsite article are now required to get their basic concept(s) greenlighted by two experienced reviewers in the Ideas Critique forum and/or IRC chatrooms before asking for draft feedback.

Please first go to the Ideas forum or the chat, give a quick summary (for the Ideas forum, please follow the instructions in the required reading thread) of the concept you want to write up (don't link the draft unless someone requests it), and reviewers can help you make sure that your core idea is something that will be successful with the community audience.

In addition: please do not put the full text of a draft in a forum post ever. If you wish to share a draft, the best way to do so is by sharing a link to your sandbox page, which can be created here: http://scp-sandbox-3.wikidot.com/.

item.title: Re: The London Brick Incident: 2nd Draft
item.content:encoded:
Hey Sybert6000. I'll be critiquing the London Brick Incident for you.

+ Critique
– hide block
  • Narrative.

The narrative, and by proxy, the anomaly is too complicated and the article itself is far, far too long. Instead of adding complexities to the article to lengthen the narrative, you should be adding depth. Depth is a far more intriguing way to explore an article as it will allow you to explore the nuances and important details of your article rather than adding more information. Less is more in a horror-themed article.

  • Tone and language.

The tone and language used in the article is lacking at times. This is especially notable in your interview logs. Examples include:

We checked the corporal, he was dead, like I said the head was probably caved in when he was hit, I ordered my men back when one of my men called out "Captain more of them, they're moving they're moving!".

Fuck me it was like fighting off an army of bulldozers, I wouldn't even say three minutes passed before they were at the front door, at that point four men are fuck all against an army of scuffed Mr potato heads.

The Captain has just gone from callously describing the death of the men under his command to referring to instances of an unknown lifeform as Mr. Potato Heads. There's a massive clash of tone there.

More importantly than either of these, however, the article shows more than it tells. You don't need to describe in detail how the Foundation came to work out how the brick monsters came about, you should be showing this to us. The horror of an article is best left to the imagination of the reader.

Redaction should go. It has no place in the article and only detracts from the tone.

  • The anomaly.

A good anomaly is simple but deep. This is an extremely convoluted and complex anomaly that lacks any real depth. I'd strip back the extraneous elements of the anomaly and focus on the core.

I was especially intrigued by the idea that it was made on accident by the Brick Company attempting to cut corners in the brick-making process. This is something you could explore in more depth.

  • Overall.

I love the idea. Brick fungus monsters are cool and pretty terrifying. However, the execution leaves something to be desired in the finished product. The autopsy report is definitely the best part of the article and there's lots of information that you've put in the description that can be moved there.

Always remember that a narrative has a beginning, middle, and end. You want to move the reader through each stage by increasing the tension, drama, or horror with each and every single sentence. Here, the autopsy should act as your middle by heightening the horror and tension.

item.title: SCP Concept: "This Last Week"
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Drama/Emotional, possibly a little Horror (I think - hard to pin down)

Page Layout: Nothing incredibly special at this stage. If this ends up being my first published article, I don't want to be too ambitious and not be able to follow through without experience first.

Elevator Pitch: Time loop, town repeating for decades. No-one in town's aware it's happening.

Central Narrative: Loop - when first documented - lasted 1 week, resetting at midnight (internal date noted, but when undecided).

Log of events in cycle, taken not long into repeats. Includes local activities. Occasional person enters - unfortunates from before containment who didn't get out in time (e.g. Sole car enters. Driver confused because brother was in car in front, implying brother left town pre-midnight, while he didn't).

Affected bubble's temporal hazard, as anyone who enters becomes trapped in repeats if they don't leave pre-reset, arrival happening every time (shown with unfortunate agent). Living things from town cannot be removed, disappearing when extracted. Non-living objects can be, however, duplicates taking their place next repeat. Objects/people introduced from outside arrive at same time in later loops.

Speculated to be unstable spacetime bubble, causing repeats and leaking details from other realities, overwriting native. No cause determined.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Subtle changes between loops - only couple tiny things in given repeat (e.g. teapot's colour or someone's breakfast). Small things eventually snowball into drastic shifts over countless cycles - e.g. street names, businesses and even identities (extreme example's bartender originally documented as male replaced by woman). Log of noted changes over time provided, starting out with small things before they're moved to unseen comprehensive file, log's remainder focusing on significant alterations.

Article end: Researcher contacts superior. Too subtle to tell before, but they're now sure loop's shrinking. Not physical space, but timeframe, and events aren't exiting the loop - they're compressing, events getting closer together and causing problems. Example: Car driving through crossroads, another driving from other road seconds after. Compressed, crossings get closer until cross at same time, and either stop or crash. Regardless, it's a major change, causing butterflies. They speculate that as bubble grows increasingly unstable, timeframe will keep shrinking, events compacting until "casual density event" occurs. It's anybody's guess what happens then. As it isn't accelerating, however - and week's only shortened by minutes in decades - it's centuries before "event". It's suggested personnel prepare in case something emerges sooner.

'Emerges' is deliberate wording. Speculation that distortion/timeline leakage caused by something pushing into our reality.

Compression's resulted in short calm immediately pre-midnight, where there's no more events. Town disappears temporarily, leaving semi-circular crater. Was emergence of this that revealed compression.

Additional Notes: Still trying to get SCP approved, so any feedback's good.

item.title: Re: Writing my first SCP
item.content:encoded:
Hi there!
So, the biggest problem you have here is the lack of a narrative or a real hook. You gave the barest description of the physical appearance of this entity and… that's it. I know you might want to keep some info up your sleeve to make a great reveal for those reading the article but this is not the moment to surprise the audience. The goal of this forum is to help you polish your idea and take it to the highest standards possible before going to the main page.
What is this entity's story? Does it have objectives, allegiances, a backstory or an important information to contribute to the Foundation? This is the moment to define and explore these questions, you can write the mysterious bits and alluring questions later.
Also, the Norse accent is not a hook, it is a quirk of the entity. A hook would be a connection to real life events or other events on the SCP universe, a new character or plotline to be explored on other articles and tales, a reference to folklore or mythology, etc.

I hope you figure out how to flesh out this concept and make it a nice article!

item.title: Re: The Friendly Shadow
item.content:encoded:
I have not got anything on the main site, but here are my thoughts anyway - take these with a grain of salt. If you don't like a proposed change, feel free to ignore it.

+ > Line by Line < 
- Close


Things I would remove will be crossed out and Things I would add will be underlined, and things that could be decided by you [E.g specifics] are in [Square brackets]

Description

SCP-XXXX is the shadow of XXXX-1, Clarence Carter

I would change to

SCP-XXXX is the shadow of XXXX-1, a humanoid appearing as a [middle-aged] male of [indeterminent] descent. SCP-XXXX-1 self-identifies as Clarence Carter.

XXXX is a sapient shadow with the outlines of a mouth, eyes, and entire body which moves whenever active.

I would change to

SCP-XXXX is a sapient shadow with the has outlines of a mouth, eyes, and entire body which moves whenever active. The eyes and mouth appear as illuminated regions within the shadow.

This fixes some clinical tone issues, and makes the appearance clearer, I think.

XXXX has no way of talking to people outside of XXXX-1

Is not clinical. I would change it to

SCP-XXXX can communicate with SCP-XXXX-1 but is incapable of communicating with other organisms.

Stretching itself, XXXX is able to change into different forms.

Again, Clinical tone is off here.

SCP-XXXX is relatively amorphous, stretching and morphing into various forms at will.

XXXX can detach itself from XXXX-1 to interact with shadows of objects or people.

As well as changing XXXX and XXXX-1 to SCP-XXXX and SCP-XXXX-1 respectively, I would add the following for clarity.

XXXX can detach itself from XXXX-1 to interact with shadows of objects or people. Interactions with these shadows correspond to movements with the objects casting them.

Subject has only left XXXX-1 on rare occasions. Reasons are unknown. More information under Addendum XXXX.

Should be changed to something like:

Subject SCP-XXXX has only left loses contact with SCP-XXXX-1 on rare occasions. Reasons are unknown The cause of these incidents are unknown. More information under Addendum XXXX. For more information, see Addenda.

Discovery

SCP-XXXX's discovery was on December 3ed, 20██ in Charleston, West Virginia. XXXX-1's apprehension by authorities after breaking into the West Virginia State Museum made It clear that his shadow was nonexistent. Put into the police database, the Foundation took subject from custody for investigation. Two hours later, (after interrogation with XXXX-1) XXXX was contained by MTF Iota-10 ("Damn Feds"), with both subjects receiving their numbers.

Has some SPAG errors and poor phrasing, which I would recommend changing to this:

SCP-XXXX's discovery was SCP-XXXX was discovered on December 3erd, 20██ in Charleston, West Virginia. XXXX-1's apprehension by authorities after breaking into the West Virginia State Museum made It clear that his shadow was nonexistent. SCP-XXXX-1 was apprehended after breaking into Virginia State Museum. Following its arrest, it became clear that the entities shadow was non-existent. At this point, embedded foundation agents reported the anomaly and anesticised witnesses as necessary. Put into the police database, the Foundation took the subject from custody for investigation. _SCP-XXXX-1 was interrogated in foundation custody following its discovery. Two hours later, SCP-XXXX was contained by MTF Iota-10 ("Damn Feds"). The two objects were designated as SCP-XXXX shortly after.__(after interrogation with XXXX-1) XXXX was contained by MTF Iota-10 ("Damn Feds"), with both subjects receiving their numbers

Addendum XXXX.1

XXXX and XXXX-1 go through testing everyday at Six PM, testing the capabilities of XXXX's limitations. XXXX-1 frequently asks XXXX for advice and is a translator for tests. All investigation on XXXX-1's Family has come back with no results.

This phrasing unclear, and the sentence structure is a bit muddled. I would maybe change this to:

Following its discovery, SCP-XXXX and SCP-XXXX-1 were sent through a round of testing, which was designed to gauge SCP-XXXX's capabilities. On-site personnel have noted that SCP-XXXX-1 and SCP-XXXX regularly communicate, with SCP-XXXX-1 asking SCP-XXXX for personal advice, including discussions of SCP-XXXX-1's containment, and apparent amnesia. It should also be noted that investigation into the family or prior life of SCP-XXXX has been inconclusive.

This version establishes -1's 'amnesia' earlier, while also flowing a bit nicer (this is coming from a biased opinion though).

Foreword: The Interview was an attempt to uncover any origin/information of SCP-XXXX. The questions went without incident and both SCP-XXXX and -1 complied.

It should probably be noted here that -1 refers to XXXX as 'Thomas' as it introduces minor-confusion later on.

In terms of the interview in itself, I'll give my thoughts on the style in the 'Overall' section, but since I am horrible at writing dialogue, I'll just point out any typos I spotted.

<The desk would suddenly break apart, one of the limbs giving way. Review of the footage showed XXXX caused this for unknown reasons. Dr. Rose calls maintenance to replace the desk. The interview continued shortly after>

I don't see why this line's here. This doesn't really add much to the story, as far as I can tell. If you need to keep it in though, change it to:

<The desk would suddenly break apart, one of the limbs giving way. The desk breaks apart suddenly, with one leg collapsing. Review of the footage showed XXXX caused this for unknown reasons. show that SCP-XXXX caused this by interacting with the shadow of the desk. SCP-XXXX's motivations for this are unknown. Dr. Rose calls maintenance to replace the desk. The interview continued continues shortly after>

No, the police to me first.

You mean 'The police took me first'?

No luck. We’ve traveled half of America with no luck.

Maybe

"No luck. We travelled across half of America, still nothing"

SCP-XXXX: "I’m sorry, what? Am I being separated from Thomas?"

Do you mean SCP-XXXX-1?

SCP-XXXX: "Are you saying that I’m not being compliant now?"

Same here.

<Thomas appears to say something, Clarence looking over.>

Shouldn't this be 'SCP-XXXX' for thomas, and 'SCP-XXXX-1' for Clarence? Also, Interview transcripts are in the present tense, so it should be 'SCP-XXXX-1 looks over'.

<Thomas appears to speak over Clarence, Clarence going silent.>

Same applies here.

Expermiment Logs

I'm just gonna say it here, but the experiment logs seem to be kind of… useless? It kind of seems like a sudden, random shift from the main narrative rather than something useful. I would just specify some bits about how the anomaly works (like seeing in 2D) in the description.

Update XXXX

After further investigation in the State Museum where SCP-XXXX was found, Agent Hart found Agent Wolf had disappeared while examining a painting on exhibit. Item has been taken for further investigation. Most certainly has a connection to SCP-XXXX.

I would describe the painting here. Also, maybe change 'Most certainly' to 'It is believed this painting has a connection to SCP-XXXX

Interview XXXX.4

The same thing applies as with the interview above.

<Subject gives a smile>

Maybe just "SCP-XXXX smiles."

<XXXX swiftly wrote two giant letters on the second page, taking the whole paper up>

I would change to

<SCP-XXXX writes two large letters on the second page, covering the paper.>

<XXXX appears grief stricken>

Is unclinical. Maybe say

<SCP-XXXX appears distressed>

Interview XXXX-6

I DON'T HAVE A FAMILY, I DON'T HAVE AMNESIA, AND THOMAS IS JUST A FUCKING LIAR!"

I don't know if a transcription would emphasise text in upper case to show shouting, but that's just me.

Dr. Doxon: "…"

Should change to

<Dr. Doxon remains silent.>

Closing Statement: SCP-XXXX-1 has gone into forms of irritation and depression. Upon going through a psych eval, it was concluded that XXXX-1's IQ is 80, and while being in the body of a man in his early 30s, he has the mental intelligence of a teenager.

Could be changed to

Following Interview XXXX-6, SCP-XXXX-1 has been diagnosed with anxiety and clinical depression. Psychiatric evaluation by foundation also concluded that SCP-XXXX-1 has experienced a significantly stunted psychiatric development. Based on these findings, the Intelligence Quotient (IQ) of the subject has been determined as 80, with a mental age of 15.

Or something of the like.

Final Update

+ XXXX's Message

Maybe should be

+ Open File

The inside of the message is fine as far as I can tell.

+ > Overall < 
- Close

Overall, this article is a bit meh… The emotional core of the article doesn't really hit for me, as I just don't feel invested in these two characters. I would replace the experiment logs with a bit of communication between the anomaly, in order to show their personalities when together.

The Article also lacks a hook, with a pretty stock standard opening. This is by no means bad, but It could be improved by adding an update to the containment procedures saying "Following incident XXXX.1 (the discovery of the painting), SCP-XXXX-1 has been provided with counselling and further educational within [Site-102]1." This addition serves to give the reader a hint of what to expect from the article. I would also add the painting discovered as SCP-XXXX-2, describing it nebulously as 'SCP-XXXX-2 is a painting showing a silhouetted humanoid figure standing on a hill. Further information is limited to personnel above level 3 clearance.' Then maybe add a 'LEVEL 3 CLEARANCE REQUIRED - INPUT CREDENTIALS' over the discovery of SCP-XXXX-2. This hooks the reader without spoiling the mystery.

Other stuff I noted, the interviews dialogue feels a bit… weird? -1 doesn't really have an established personality, and XXXX itself is… so bad at lying its silly. Furthermore; the speech just doesn't strike me as … realistic? I don't know how to describe it, but it seems just weirdly worded. If the researchers noted this, it could add more to the idea that SCP-XXXX-1 was created from nothing, but to me it feels unitentional. Karablue may be able to suggest proper changes to the interviews.

With a few changes however, I think this could be really good. I'd recommend reading some other emotional articles to see what works, and revising the story to flow better. But again, this doesn't strike me as a 'first author series one-clone', rather having actual substance behind it. Good luck if you managed to get through this wall of text!

P.S: Once you have revised the article, feel free to PM me again, and I'll check it over again. Good luck with getting this on the site.

Footnotes
1. It can be literally any site, but you know what I mean

item.title: Re: A new SCP I'm working on
item.content:encoded:
Hi there, I am not an official critter but let me share some thoughts here.

First off, you must remember that the Foundation is cold, not cruel. Why would they continue testing on the boy when the effects of his anomalous abilities are clear from the beginning? They would hardly go past one or two tests and once they were sure this is a child who happens to return from the dead they would keep him in custody in a somewhat nice cell and call it a day. That's what was done to 053 herself.

If the bulk of your narrative was just testing logs then you don't really have a narrative yet. Few people would be interested in reading about a child being tortured. The narrative needs a progression, an arc, maybe it can be the boy telling his life, or the efforts of a researcher to find the boy's family or what is left of them. The readers must feel something when reading your article, you must define what it is you want them to feel and then write around it. If your goal is to make us feel sorry for the boy I still suggest approaching it on a less gratuitously violent way.

Good luck on your writing!

item.title: Re: Men Are Expendable
item.content:encoded:
No Greenlight. After some fairly extensive attempts to search, the only evidence I can find of this supposed myth is literally all connected to Ripley's Believe It or Not, the same source that made people think that Einstein failed math. There might be a myth about this topic that's not coming up because it's buried in an obscure anthropological journal somewhere, but when the basis for an SCP is the word of a bunch of hucksters, it's kind of hard to take this seriously.

And there's a kind of skeevy tilt to this whole idea that I have trouble putting into words. Language like children from a 'secret tribe' possessing 'incredible strength, intelligence and a great cognitive capacity' comes off as… I don't know what but it doesn't sound great.

item.title: Re: Omelette of Misfortunate Death
item.content:encoded:
Hey there PillsburyDough, I’ll be critting your idea today!
Note that I am neither particularly experienced nor an official reviewer (but I am a flight officer), so take everything I say with a grain of salt. With that being said, let’s begin the (brief) crit!
Disclaimer: I am currently on mobile, so the formatting may be a bit iffy and the crit won’t be as long.

+ Open Crit +
- Close Crit -

So my biggest problem with this concept is that it’s simply SCP-1137 but an omelette. Unfortunate that you happened to come up with an idea that is very similar to (almost eggsactly the same as) one already on the site, but it can happen to anyone.

Also, this:

Their brains become scrambled.

Nice pun. Not fowl at all, and that’s no yolk. It cracked me up, one could say. I may poach that pun for later, should the opportunity arise. But I digress. I can’t spend all my time shelling out bad puns.

I’d recommend checking out the Guide Hub it you haven’t already, and also the Tag Search as a checking mechanism to make sure something like this doesn’t happen again.

Anyway, that’s my crit. Thanks for reading, and I hope this helps!
P.S I’m sorry for the puns.
P.P.S No I’m not. They were EGGSellent.

item.title: Omelette of Misfortunate Death
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): OMELETTE

Elevator Pitch:
An omelette is discovered. Delicious. Many guards and researchers at the foundation go mad over this beautiful omelette.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative:
An omelette is discovered on the top of a statue, in the middle of a small town, in Oregon. People begin going mad for omelettes around the area. People begin dying due to over omeletting. A threat is posed. Anyone who sees the omelette becomes crazed with trying to recreated an omelette just as beautiful. No one who tries succeeds. They become mad with failure. Their brains become scrambled. What must they do to create the perfect Omelette without dying? The foundation becomes involved after a whole town dies of starvation with in a matter of days. The town had an ample food source. How did they die with all the omelettes? The source they find is this SCP. The foundation takes the omelette into confinement. They begin tests and find several interesting facts about the omelette, such as, it does not decompose. They begin to question whether or not its sentient. Many misfortunate tests happen until researchers at the foundation finally find a good use for this SCP.

Attention Getter:
Is the Omelette sentient? It's a Omelette for peat sakes, that at least sparks my attention. Will the omelette take over the world if it escapes or will it plunge everyone around it into immediate cooking failures and death?
Additional notes:
I am currently waiting on my original SCP idea to be critiqued so I decided to add another strange idea. I am new and again no matter how harsh, I would still enjoy criticism!

item.title: A new SCP I'm working on
item.content:encoded:
Scp 5091 is a boy who died in 1909 but came back to life in his coffin. He suffocated from lack of air, then came back. This went on until the cemetery he was buried in was dug up and he was taken in by the foundation, who conducted a battery of tests on him to see how different causes of death would affect him.

I call him Ressurection Teddy, as a nod to the legend of Resurrection Mary. Does that count as plagiarism?

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: This kid isn't any stronger than a normal child, and he can be killed just the same, but nothing will keep him down permanently, even if it takes months for him to recover.

Central Narrative: The different ways the foundation killed him. They've starved him, kept him up for a few months, froze him, burned him, cut him up, poisoned him, introduced him to other Scps such as 053 and 049, and even given him a dish containing shrimp, only to realize he's deathly allergic to the stuff when he went into anaphylactic shock.

But no matter what happens, he'll come back. Often times he's confused or frightened or just plain pissed, but alive and free of any fatal wounds nonetheless. All these tests have left him traumatized, possibly beyond repair.

During an interview, he asks where his parents are. The doctor tells him they're likely dead, and he has a panic attack and hasn't talked since. Testing was suspended, and the poor thing is being given counseling.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: He can't be killed permanently, at least not in any way that the foundation has discovered.

Additional Notes: The 5091 number is a placeholder, I'll give it another number when I post it to the mainsite.

item.title: Re: Shepherd boy
item.content:encoded:
[+] Some additional thoughts for you
– hide block

I do have to admit, once i finished the writing i read it about fifty times and every time there’s something that felt out of place or unnecessary but I didn’t know how to approach it. ( got scared to trim it.)

IMO: just trim it.

The central core or what i’m really trying to say through the article would be learning who you really are or having peace with you inner conflict and finding power from it. Once the inner peace is achieved no one can really stop you or tell you that your wrong, but the society as a whole always finds a loop hole on the idea. So I guess i didn’t really made it clear.

I think the central problem with the article, in terms of achieving this at the moment, is that this journey to find peace with your inner conflict isn't actually what the story is about? Like, the Foundation swoops in after it happens, so this like, intimate, personal struggle isn't shown; and instead we have this kinda, overview of what happened as a result of it happening?

My suggestion would be to do one of two things: either make this a tale, or start this sooner in the story.

In the first, you'd be radically changing the PoV so it'd be from SCP-XXXX-1's perspective, and entirely centred around them being put in a place where they're forced to find the peace within them, or in a place where finding that peace is their entire struggle, and the story would unfold as they gradually begin to find it while stuff around them gets worse; and the resolution would likely be when the Foundation comes in an interferes or something.

In the second, the focus would be the Foundation locking up -1 just as he's starting to gain this inner power, and so the central conflict would be around this boy trying to achieve the peace he needs whilst the Foundation are doing everything that they can to stop it: the ending would likely be the boy escaping to form the cave and the peaceful area, instead of that being the start. Like pacing would probably look something like "Foundation grabs minor reality bender; reality bender gets stronger; Foundation does stuff to try and stop this; bender keeps getting more powerful; bender escapes and creates a place of peace, as a mirror to the place of conflict that was the foundation for him".

item.title: Re: SCP Idea: {Redacted}
item.content:encoded:
My thoughts - Note: I am not an experienced reviewer, and cannot give greenlights.

+ Show
- Hide

I hope it hasn't been done before.

Unfortunately, this idea has been done before - notably in SCP-055, but also in SCP-579 and SCP-5790. The idea of an anomaly with information being anomalously hard to gain is already called 'antimemetics' - a pretty well-explored concept on the wiki - but that doesn't mean a concept like this wouldn't work. For starters, expand your concept. It's hard to review a story without elaboration on the storyline, as even a bland anomaly can have an interesting storyline. Secondly, see what works in other antimemetic articles. In the articles I gave, its the information they do have, not the information they don't, that makes them interesting - the use of bizarre containment procedures hint at a threat that cant be talked about, and so on. I wouldn't recommend doing these formulas exactly, but try and do something interesting with the concept of a self-redacting anomaly. Finally; if you are gonna go down a comedic route, I just don't think 'so what is it?' will work very well, as the idea has already been used seriously a ton, so it doesn't mesh well, for experienced readers - but that's just my opinion. If you revise this idea, feel free to PM me, and I'll look over it again.

Hope that helps!

There are some questions it should answer:

Does the entity behaves the same, as if part of the video, or does it change in behaviour each time?

How does the affected subject reacts to the video throughout it? The description says only the subject orgasms at the end, but the sample occurrences imply unconsciousness and something else far before the end.

Why isn't there some tests to show what happens to subjects during the video? And why they didn't try to contain the entity instead of harming it?

In particular for the later paragraph describing it as just acquired and the shooting as accidental, unavoidable or done by a third party would help to reconcile the story with the idea of it being at Foundation custody now.

For now, downvoted.

item.title: Forum Criticism Team - Captain Post
item.content:encoded:
Author, per the Draft Forum's new policy: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-10629348/new-draft-forum-policies authors who have not yet posted a successful mainsite article are now required to get their basic concept(s) greenlighted by two experienced reviewers in the Ideas Critique forum and/or IRC chatrooms before asking for draft feedback.

Please first go to the Ideas forum or the chat, give a quick summary (for the Ideas forum, please follow the instructions in the required reading thread) of the concept you want to write up (don't link the draft unless someone requests it), and reviewers can help you make sure that your core idea is something that will be successful with the community audience.

During the conceptualization stage, reviewers can also help by letting you know if something similar already exists on the site, and/or telling you if there are any cliches/pitfalls/other typical downvote reasons to be careful of with your particular idea. These issues are more effectively addressed earlier on in the writing process.

If you have already received the requisite greenlights, please note from whom and where you received them. If you would like to receive draft critique without going through the greenlighting process, please use the IRC chatrooms to request reviews.
